reviews.comment: He's really engaging during lectures and genuinely cares if students are following along.
Dr. Tamamis brings so much energy and genuine passion to the classroom. The posted material is very helpful, but sometimes calls on students to keep everyone engaged and involved.

The class often prioritizes presentation over substance. Many of the word documents use obviously AI-generated images, which frequently feel unnecessary rather than helpful for understanding the material. The professor is always extremely enthusiastic, but after a while it comes across as performative rather than genuinely engaging!!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell he cares very much about his students and how he wants everyone to succeed. His lectures were sometimes confusing as he would talk very fast at times so it be difficult to keep track of where in the lecture slides he was at. He gives out so so many examples in the notes & showed past exams for review that aligned with the exam material

If Dr. Tamamis learns your name he will call on you every single class to ask questions. Attendance is mandatory due to random quizzes/attendance. You will not understand what happens in lecture but Exams are very similar to HW. Exams are graded on answers not work so easy to miss a lot of points if you make a simple mistake.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Please don't take this class with him

Exams are very similar to homework and in-class problems, so they are fair with practice. He moves quickly through slides, so reviewing notes beforehand helps. Some problems require programmable calculators, so familiarize yourself with transferring code to calculators. Also, when he says to study derivations, please do it. You will need them.
Please save yourself. No curve bc too many sweaty people got 100s. whomp whomp
The lectures and exams can be confusing, so students should be prepared for a significant amount of independent study.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were engaging and the prof gave many example problems making thermo easy to understand.
Very motivating and caring instructor. Lectures were well structured and organized with lots of interaction.
just pray that he shouldnt teach thermo guysss....
Really good at confusing the students. Better to self study
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I mostly have to read the textbook and do self-study. The lectures were not helpful and lots of unnecessary yelling random words. He likes to challenge students to show superiority rather than trying to teach. Wish I could take another prof.

Very caring professor but will call-out students in-class if he gets to know your name. Does not always understand in-class questions due to somewhat of a language barrier (still understandable though). Based off 4 exams (35% final) and homeworks are very long, but welcome to being an engineer. You will have to teach yourself most material.

Dr. Tamamis provided great and engaging lectures for such a difficult course, and it was clear that he wanted to help us students to succeed. The most frustrating part though was how long he took to grade exams. In a course that builds on itself so much, it would have been helpful to have more timely feedback.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Midterms are of medium difficulty but he does not give helpful reviews. He did not teach the last three chapters well and assigned very few additional problems/homework to study for these chapters. He answers questions terribly and his office hours are unhelpful. He will just say you should understand thermo better or make fewer mistakes.

A bad lecturer and doesn't give review material, but the tests are often similar to the homework problems though. If asked questions in class he will usually misunderstand the question or refuse to answer. I would not take him unless necessary.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kind of unapproachable, but very passionate. Took forever to grade exams, often, we would not receive past exam grades until the week of the following exam. Would randomly call on students in lecture, so be prepared for that. Overall good, exams are a lot like practice problems given in class.

He gives thorough lectures. Very knowledgeable of the subjects and wants students to do well. No partial credit on HWs or exams, even if you make a simple mistake and its clear you work the problems correctly. Calls on people in class and is a little off putting in how he handles interactions. Curves well.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is good at teaching you stuff during lectures but on exam and homework's he gives zero partial credit and refuses to change anything. Stay away from him if at all possible.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Materials is not a hard class and most of the problems are just plugging numbers into formulas so it's pretty hard to fail or do bad imo. However, tamamis can grade very hard with limited partial credit so always make sure to double check your answers or you'll lose a lot of points for simple mistakes.

Never written a review but had to for him. Tamamis is the worst prof I've had. Grades extremely hard with no partial credit. Feels like he is above his students and it shows. Don't bother asking for help as he is condescending in & out of class. Dropped to take class from someone else after he told me to rethink my career when I went in for help.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. When a homework assignment asks you to sketch, you need to assume that you have to sketch, calculate, describe, and explain your answer. You can't simply answer the question that is asked but you must read his mind and the supposed grading rubric. He will not change any grades even if the grading was unfair and incorrect.

He's a very passionate and engaging lecturer which helped me learn the material better during the lecture.  Also, he goes over problems very similar to the ones on tests in class so you should have a pretty good idea of what will be on the tests.
The lectures were interesting and engaging and the professor made the material easy to understand.

I didn't find lectures to be helpful, but they were mandatory cause attendance is a small portion of your grade. He's not allowed to help you with the HW before they're due, but they're not that hard. The exams are very similar to the in-class examples and HW. One page of cheat sheet allowed on each midterm, and 3 pages were allowed on the final.

Best way to prepare for the tests is to do the HW problems and lecture problems over and over. Always had sign-ins/in-class quizzes so you have to go to lectures. Lectures are fast so you have to teach yourself. Oustide help sessions were very useful. I felt unprepared for the final though. He was passionate and provided a solid curve at end.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CHEN 205 during Spring Semester. Prof Tamamis is passionate during the lectures. He likes to keep the class engaged by calling on students. Attendance is taken often. The midterm exams are very similar to the homework assignments so study those very well. The final exam was very challenging. Gave a very generous curve at the end!

Dr. Tamamis is a bit unpredictable. He appears very passionate and caring, but it felt hard to approach him because of the way he answered questions. His midterm exams were very similar to homework, but he is a very strict grader. It felt like he didn't prepare us for the final at all. If you take him for thermo, prepare to learn things yourself.

I loved this class. He was always engaging with the students and asking questions to make sure we understood the concepts. He made access for help in the class available every weekday with his TAs and himself. He wants to see his students succeed. The homework was pretty similar to the exams and he does plenty of practice problems as well
Professor made the class very interesting throughout the course. Homework and examples solved in class were helpful.

Horrible, horrible professor, I had him for Chen 205 and Chen 322, lectures are very boring and not interactive at all just throws questions on the board and tries to explain them but doesn't actually run through them. The grading of tests is very weird sometimes gives partial credit sometimes doesn't.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor I've ever had. Man barely gives partial credit for any of his tests and then complains that his students are doing bad. He also doesn't excuse anything so if you miss an assignment he just gives you a zero. Class is so boring I started playing chess just so I don't fall asleep. Avoid this prof

This class wasn't very hard, but he did his best to make it hard, you were given no partial credit for the test and his lectures were boring and never-ending. He is very caring and nice but when you give him a suggestion or anything that might mean he was wrong he will treat you like you are stupid I didn't enjoy his class
His teaching is very good and he clearly describes all concepts by using example problems. Would definitely take again.

Tests are most of the class and are based off homework. Do the homework and you should get an A, one of the tests sunk me to a B but upon later reflection I realized it was similar to a homework problem and the problem was worth 50 points. His lectures are useless, just zone them out, read the book and do the homework several times to prepare.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Does NOT answer questions in class. Period. He is quite helpful in office hours though, and had 3 TA's & a help session weekly. Class moves insanely fast, so you really have to read the material from the book. If you won't have time to go to office hours, you're going to have a hard time.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures go by really fast and he doesn't usually answer students' questions until the end and because of that, it's often hard to understand. He'd pick on students in front of the class to make sure they knew stuff which is an embarrassment for a lot. Tests are easy if you do homework but he's just a really bad incomprehensible teacher. Periodt.

Dr. Tamamis is a great person, he really wants to teach his students well and make them successful. However, the homework system is a little unfair and he does not give partial credits. Dr. Tamamis lectures really fast so it is very hard for a lot of students to catch up.

Thermo I is a hard class for almost everyone. Dr. Tamamis does a pretty good job of teaching the material and is very nice and engaging. Exams are easy and based off the assigned homework, but be prepared to study and go to office hours.
The course is well organized, and the instructor is excellent and very helpful.

Possibly the most useless professor of all time. Attendance is mandatory so I advise you show up, zone out, and read the textbook on your own time. He is incapable of teaching anything relevant to the test in class, often places emphasis unnecessary work during the test. The reason his rating is so high is because he's "passionate."
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate and enjoys teaching. I would take this class again.
Always willing to answer questions and fair in grading.
Bad

Professor Tamamis really cares about his students. He puts a lot of effort to make difficult concepts clear and understandable by the students. He is always open to questions. The homeworks are quite demanding but the exams are quite similar to the homeworks so they become easy. He also grades fairly.

No partial credit, just reads from the textbook for lecture, doesn't answer questions, doesn't ever post grades online or hand back all assignments/ quizzes, doesn't explain topics well, makes analogies that just make people more confused, and thinks saying "please understand" or "technically" make students understand better. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Interesting material, but professor made it a bad experience. I ended up reading the book, which helped way more than lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy i guess, but isnt good at conveying ideas well and often makes stuff way more confusing than it should be. Wasnt that hard of a class but i did not have a good time
Says he tries his best to help students, then refuses to listen to any feedback or give actual answers to questions.
Bad prof, unfair grading, don't take if you can avoid

The tests were exactly like examples from class and the homework which made them pretty easy. You need to pick where you sit in class carefully because he doesn't use a microphone and it can be difficult to hear sometimes. Also if he decides to write on the board... forget it. You won't see what it says unless you're right there.

WORST PROF I HAVE EVER HAD. I am an A student and this profs communication skills/class set up is a big part of the reason I am getting a B (maybe a C). He talks toward the back of the class so it is hard to hear him. But even if I did hear, he can take forever and he still doesn't make his vague explanations clear. seriously the worst

He means well, but he is not a good communicator which makes this easy class take more time than with other profs. His random analogies, unconventional explanations, and overall vague answers to specific questions make you super confused and forces you to spend additional time to review/teach yourself outside of class. Good person, bad communicator
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Tamamis means well, but he is not the best lecturer. His lecures were extremely fast, and he never fully worked out example problems in class. Provides tons of help outside of class through help sessions and TAs, which I found more helpful than going to his office hours. Exams were almost identical to the homework, and he curves his exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Tamamis is a super caring professor. He loves his students and teaching. However, his lectures can be difficult to follow as he moves quickly and makes frequent assumptions without explanation. I feel like I did not obtain a solid understanding of thermodynamics and wish I had put more time into reading the textbook and understanding the topics
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Tamamis works examples on the board and gives homework problems that are similar to the exams. However, when you have a question in class, be ready to hold onto it for a while. He can come across as rude when not answering questions during class. He is not very helpful during office hours. Go to his TA's help sessions & do the homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've never had a profcare about me as much as Dr. Tamamis. He goes out of his way and cares about each student. Hes known as the super passionate and enthusiastic prof in Thermo. This can be bad sometimes since he talks super fast with his accent so take notes fast. Other than that, his test are  super fair and grades super fairly.
Dr. Tamamis is the sweetest professor I've had in the chemical engineering department so far. From day one he is concerned about the students and their learning of thermodynamics.

The most caring and sincere professor in the entire department. He really wants students to enjoy and find an interest in the course. Always prepared for class and never late. Loves to answer questions and create discussion among students. Great chance discuss big ideas in thermo. I took his elective course - Biomolecular Simulations and Design
